questions.q: Who will stir up the Egyptians?
questions.a: Yahweh will stir up the Egyptians.

questions.q: What country is this message about?
questions.a: This message is about Egypt.

questions.q: Who will the Egyptians be stirred up against?
questions.a: They will be stirred up against each other.

questions.q: From whom will the Egyptians seek help when they are confused?
questions.a: They will seek help from idols, fortunetellers, and those who try to contact the dead.

questions.q: Who will Yahweh cause to lead the Egyptians?
questions.a: Yahweh will deliver Egypt into the hand of a hard master, and a fierce king will rule over them.

questions.q: What will happen to the waters of Egypt?
questions.a: The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will become dry.

questions.q: What will happen to the rivers and streams of Egypt?
questions.a: The rivers will become foul, the streams will dry up, and the reeds and rushes will wither.

questions.q: What will happen to the plants growing along the Nile?
questions.a: They will dry up and be blown away by the wind.

questions.q: What will the fishermen do when they can no longer catch fish in the Nile?
questions.a: The fishermen will mourn and grieve.

questions.q: What will happen to the cloth workers in Egypt?
questions.a: The cloth workers will feel ashamed because they have no work.

questions.q: What will happen to the people who work for wages in Egypt?
questions.a: They will feel great distress.

questions.q: What has happened to the counsel of Pharaoh’s counselors?
questions.a: Their counsel has become foolish.

questions.q: What should Egypt’s wise men know and tell the people?
questions.a: They should know and tell the people what Yahweh of Armies has planned against Egypt.

questions.q: Who has led Egypt astray?
questions.a: The foolish officials of Zoan and Noph, the leaders of Egypt’s tribes, have led Egypt astray.

questions.q: Why has the counsel of Pharaoh’s counselors become senseless?
questions.a: Their counsel has become senseless because Yahweh has mixed a spirit of confusion into Egypt’s midst.

questions.q: What will anyone in Egypt, whether important or unimportant, be able to do?
questions.a: Whether important or unimportant, no one will be able to do anything to change the situation.

questions.q: In that day, what will the Egyptians be like?
questions.a: In that day, the Egyptians will not be strong warriors. They will tremble with fear.

questions.q: How will the Egyptians feel about the land of Judah?
questions.a: The Egyptians will be very afraid of Judah.

questions.q: In that day, what will five cities in Egypt do?
questions.a: They will swear allegiance to Yahweh of Armies.

questions.q: In that day, what will be in the middle of the land of Egypt?
questions.a: In that day, there will be an altar to Yahweh in the middle of the land of Egypt.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do when the Egyptians cry out to him because of their oppressors?
questions.a: Yahweh will send them a great savior who will deliver them.

questions.q: How will the Egyptians worship Yahweh in that day?
questions.a: They will worship him with sacrifices and offerings, and they will make vows to Yahweh and keep them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do after he strikes Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh will heal Egypt after they return to him.

questions.q: In that day, who will worship Yahweh together?
questions.a: The Egyptians and the Assyrians will worship Yahweh together.

questions.q: In that day, who will be a blessing in the midst of the earth?
questions.a: Israel, Egypt and Assyria will be a blessing in the midst of the earth.

questions.q: What three nations will Yahweh bless?
questions.a: Yahweh will bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel.

commentary.text: Judgments upon Egypt. (Is. 19:1-17) Its deliverance, and the conversion of the people. (Is. 19:18-25)

Is. 19:1-17 God shall come into Egypt with his judgments. He will raise up the causes of their destruction from among themselves. When ungodly men escape danger, they are apt to think themselves secure; but evil pursues sinners, and will speedily overtake them, except they repent. The Egyptians will be given over into the hand of one who shall rule them with rigour, as was shortly after fulfilled. The Egyptians were renowned for wisdom and science; yet the Lord would give them up to their own perverse schemes, and to quarrel, till their land would be brought by their contests to become an object of contempt and pity. He renders sinners afraid of those whom they have despised and oppressed; and the Lord of hosts will make the workers of iniquity a terror to themselves, and to each other; and every object around a terror to them.

Is. 19:18-25 The words, "In that day," do not always refer to the passage just before. At a time which was to come, the Egyptians shall speak the holy language, the Scripture language; not only understand it, but use it. Converting grace, by changing the heart, changes the language; for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. So many Jews shall come to Egypt, that they shall soon fill five cities. Where the sun was worshipped, a place infamous for idolatry, even there shall be a wonderful reformation. Christ, the great Altar, who sanctifies every gift, shall be owned, and the gospel sacrifices of prayer and praise shall be offered up. Let the broken-hearted and afflicted, whom the Lord has wounded, and thus taught to return to, and call upon him, take courage; for He will heal their souls, and turn their sorrowing supplications into joyful praises. The Gentile nations shall not only unite with each other in the gospel fold under Christ, the great Shepherd, but they shall all be united with the Jews. They shall be owned together by him; they shall all share in one and the same blessing. Meeting at the same throne of grace, and serving with each other in the same business of religion, should end all disputes, and unite the hearts of believers to each other in holy love.
